title: Ben Derusai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: The sages commonly use the expression “like the food of Ben Derusai,” as in [Shabbat 20a](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.20a.2). He was a bandit who ate his food when it was only one-third cooked. So too in [Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, at the beginning of halakhah 9](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Avodah_Zarah.2.9.2).[^1][^2]

notes.text: רה״ט is read as “at the beginning of halakhah 9.” The one-third cooking measure is retained as Hyman gives it.

The linked Bavli and Yerushalmi both use the expression “the food of Ben Derusai.” [Rashi’s gloss](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Shabbat.20a.2.1) calls him a bandit and specifies one-third cooking.
